stem: An adult client has probable sepsis and blood cultures have been ordered with empiric antimicrobial therapy. Which sequence should the nurse support?

options.A: Collect the blood cultures as soon as possible and ideally before the first antimicrobial dose, while avoiding unnecessary delay of emergency sepsis treatment.
options.B: Delay antimicrobial therapy until final blood-culture identification and susceptibility results are available.
options.C: Give the first antimicrobial dose before collecting blood cultures because prior antibiotic exposure improves culture yield.
options.D: Cancel the blood cultures once empiric antibiotics are ordered because culture results no longer affect treatment decisions.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign adult guideline recommends collecting blood cultures as soon as possible and ideally before antimicrobial therapy in adults with possible, probable, or definite sepsis or septic shock. The same guideline emphasizes that sepsis and septic shock are medical emergencies and treatment and resuscitation should begin immediately. B is unsafe because definitive culture results are not required before empiric treatment when sepsis warrants antimicrobials. C reverses the recommended order and antibiotic exposure can reduce microbiologic recovery. D is incorrect because microbiologic diagnosis and susceptibility results support later antimicrobial de-escalation or narrowing.
educational_objective: In suspected adult sepsis, obtain blood cultures promptly and ideally before antimicrobials while ensuring that diagnostic sampling does not create avoidable delay in emergency treatment; use resulting microbiology to refine therapy.
source_organization: Society of Critical Care Medicine / European Society of Intensive Care Medicine, Surviving Sepsis Campaign
source_document_title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
source_locator: Diagnostics — Blood culture recommendation: for adults with possible, probable, or definite sepsis or septic shock, collect blood cultures as soon as possible and ideally before administration of antimicrobial therapy. Fluid resuscitation/initial management good-practice statement: sepsis and septic shock are medical emergencies and treatment/resuscitation should begin immediately. Antimicrobial therapy: de-escalate/narrow therapy when microbiological diagnosis and susceptibility profile are available.
source_claim_supported: For adults with suspected or confirmed sepsis, blood cultures should be collected promptly and ideally before antimicrobials, without allowing diagnostic sampling to undermine immediate emergency management; microbiology should later guide de-escalation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: obtain specimens using appropriate infection-related procedures and support timely evidence-based management of suspected infection.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — culture collection and antimicrobial sequencing in sepsis
correction_summary: Updated the source item to the new 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guideline and removed the vague claim that cultures must always precede antibiotics regardless of treatment delay. The final item preserves both priorities: prompt cultures ideally before antimicrobials and immediate emergency sepsis management.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against the newly current March 2026 SSC adult guideline rather than the superseded 2021 adult guideline.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A matches the blood-culture recommendation while preserving emergency-treatment urgency. B creates an unsafe delay. C reverses recommended sequencing. D ignores the role of culture/susceptibility in later therapy refinement.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; prompt culture collection ideally precedes antimicrobials without avoidable treatment delay.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; empiric therapy should not await final cultures when clinically indicated.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; antibiotic administration is not used to improve culture yield.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; microbiological results remain clinically useful for de-escalation.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: The wording avoids an absolute culture-first rule and explicitly balances diagnosis with emergency treatment, leaving A as the sole guideline-concordant option.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe plausible sequencing strategies in the same sepsis workflow.
audit_findings.blueprint: Specimen collection and infection-related safety procedures fit Safety and Infection Prevention and Control.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked the 2026 recommendation language and treatment-urgency statement. Removed obsolete timing assumptions and ensured the answer does not imply waiting for cultures or skipping them. No second answer remained.
